text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Stocks rose for a second straight day, as pharmaceuticals were spurred higher by rising U.S. drug stocks and market nerves were steadied by strength on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 added 43.7 points to 4,640.0.

FRANKFURT - Investors shrugged off a weak start on Wall Street to push stocks higher. The DAX-30 index jumped 42.69 points, or 1.14 percent, to 3,798.51. In after-hours trading the IBIS DAX stood at 3,819.52.
PARIS - Stocks surged to record highs, powered by gains on Wall Street, a rebound in the dollar and higher bond prices. The CAC-40 index soared 82.68 points, nearly 3 percent, to 2,867.44.
ZURICH - Swiss shares also rose to a record, with the with broad SPI index up 46.07 to a record 3,571.55, and the Swiss market index up 86.3 points to 5,662.4, also a record.
TOKYO - Stocks rose as a surprisingly strong improvement in business sentiment boosted investor optimism, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average jumped 337.34 points to 20,679.27.

HONG KONG - Stocks rose sharply following the recovery on Wall Street and brokers said the market had more upside before it closed for the handover festivities next week. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,065.02, up 174.06 points, or 1.17 percent.
SYDNEY - Shares ended near their highs, with the benchmark All Ordinaries index up 16.7 points to 2,705.1, within 10 points of its record of 2,714.2 set on June 20.

JOHANNESBURG - The all-share index ended at a record for the second consecutive session, boosted by the strong recovery on Wall Street on Tuesday and better-than-expected local inflation data. The all-share index rose 20.4 points to 7,354.0, the industrial index added 45.7 points to 8,669.9, while the gold index fell 11.2 points to 1,007.4.
